::: proof
Write $\mathbf{A} \eqdef \inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}\tp{\mX}$,
a $(p+1) \times n$ matrix that is fixed once we condition on $\mX$,
so that $\evb = \mathbf{A}\vY$.
Under @def-lm-general-form,
$\E{\vY \mid \mX} = \mX\vb$,
and because the $Y_i$ are independent with common variance $\ss$,
$\Cov{\vY \mid \mX} = \ss \bfI_n$.

For the mean,
using linearity of expectation for a fixed matrix times a random vector:

$$
\ba
\E{\evb \mid \mX}
&= \underbrace{\mathbf{A}}_{(p+1) \times n} \underbrace{\E{\vY \mid \mX}}_{n \times 1}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}
\\
&= \inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}\tp{\mX} \mX \vb
&& \text{(substitute } \mathbf{A} \text{ and } \E{\vY \mid \mX} \text{)}
\\
&= \underbrace{\bfI_{p+1}}_{(p+1) \times (p+1)} \underbrace{\vb}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&& \text{(a matrix inverse times the matrix is the identity)}
\\
&= \vb
&& \text{(identity matrix)}
\ea
$$

For the covariance,
using $\Cov{\mathbf{A}\vY} = \mathbf{A}\Cov{\vY}\tp{\mathbf{A}}$ for a fixed matrix $\mathbf{A}$,
and $\tp{\mathbf{A}} = \mX\inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}$
(because $\tp{\mX}\mX$ is symmetric, so its inverse is too):

$$
\ba
\Cov{\evb \mid \mX}
&= \underbrace{\mathbf{A}}_{(p+1) \times n}
\underbrace{\Cov{\vY \mid \mX}}_{n \times n}
\underbrace{\tp{\mathbf{A}}}_{n \times (p+1)}
&& \text{(covariance of a linear transformation)}
\\
&= \mathbf{A} \paren{\ss \bfI_n} \tp{\mathbf{A}}
&& \text{(substitute } \Cov{\vY \mid \mX} \text{)}
\\
&= \ss \mathbf{A} \bfI_n \tp{\mathbf{A}}
&& \text{(move the scalar } \ss \text{ to the front)}
\\
&= \ss \mathbf{A} \tp{\mathbf{A}}
&& \text{(multiplying by } \bfI_n \text{ changes nothing)}
\\
&= \ss \inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}\tp{\mX} \mX\inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}
&& \text{(substitute } \mathbf{A} \text{ and } \tp{\mathbf{A}} \text{)}
\\
&= \ss \bfI_{p+1} \inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}
&& \text{(a matrix inverse times the matrix is the identity)}
\\
&= \ss \inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}
&& \text{(identity matrix)}
\ea
$$
:::
